Hi, I'm Jace , and I founded Ashby's Customer Education function in 2025. We've expanded the team since then, I now lead the team and am excited to be hiring our next Program Manager!
Our team is built on a simple belief: Ashby Academy should feel like every customer's personal CSM. Regardless of tier or team size, every Ashby customer deserves content that meets them where they are — practical, accurate, and genuinely useful.

That standard shapes everything we build, and it's what's driven the development of our growing Academy courses, webinar program, and playbook library. We have ambitions to expand both the depth of our content and the formats we deliver it in, and this hire is a meaningful part of getting there.
As our next Customer Education Program Manager, you'll own customer-facing education work end to end. We're looking for someone who knows Ashby well enough to coach users on how to use it, and can translate that coaching into content that scales. You'll turn complex product workflows into clear, practical learning experiences, and partner closely with Customer Success, Product, PMM, and Recruiting Operations Consulting to make sure what we build is grounded in how customers actually work.
This is a hands-on role. You won't be setting strategy and handing it off. You'll be in the work: scoping, writing, building, reviewing, refining, and shipping.

Own net-new customer education work from concept through publication, including courses, playbooks, recordings, and other learning assets
Define the goal and shape of each learning asset — what it should help customers do, for whom, and in what format — then gather SME input, design the approach, and build it
Refresh and improve existing Academy content so it stays aligned with how Ashby actually works today
Translate complex Ashby workflows into clear, practical, outcome-oriented education — the kind that helps customers understand not just what to do, but why it matters
Partner cross-functionally with CS, Product, PMM, and RecOps Consultants to identify high-value education opportunities and get the right assets out at the right time
Contribute to the systems, standards, and workflows that help Customer Education scale while maintaining high-quality learning experiences
Help us explore adjacent formats when useful — lighter-weight tutorials, in-app guidance, and other just-in-time learning moments
Typical workload: You'll manage 2-3 new courses or major playbooks per quarter, plus ongoing refreshes and maintenance of existing content. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself (writing, recording, designing learning flows).
Examples of work you might own
Build a new Academy course that helps customers adopt a new Ashby feature or module
Turn product and SME input into a practical playbook tied to a real recruiting outcome
Record voiceover for a customer-facing learning asset
Audit and refresh an existing course after a product change so it reflects how Ashby works today
Partner with RecOps Consulting or other SMEs to build something that helps customers apply a concept, not just understand it
Experiment with lighter-weight format when a full course isn't the right answer

You already know Ashby well. You understand how its workflows are structured, where users can get stuck, and what it takes to use it effectively. Formal customer education experience isn't required. What matters is Ashby fluency and the ability to translate that into coaching and content.
Beyond your Ashby depth, you could be a great fit if you also have:
You've taught something complex before. Whether live, through writing, or both, you've helped someone understand a complicated product or process and have ideas on how to turn that into something scalable.
You can juggle multiple projects. You manage several at once without losing momentum when priorities shift.
You're a strong writer. You can make complicated things feel clear and useful on the page.
You're comfortable recording voiceovers. Recording yourself for customer-facing content feels natural, not like a stretch.
You own work end-to-end. You can take something from problem framing through build and launch without needing a fully mapped plan first.
You work well with subject matter experts. You know how to pull what you need from busy stakeholders without losing momentum or clarity.
You have good judgment about scope. You can tell when something should be deep, lightweight, or optimized for speed, and you choose intentionally.
Traditional customer education experience isn't required. The background that matters most is hands-on Ashby experience — as a recruiter, a recruiting ops practitioner, an implementation specialist, a CSM, or someone who has simply used Ashby deeply enough to teach it. If you've owned meaningful work with real autonomy, improved how something gets taught or documented, and cared about outcomes over optics, you'll likely feel at home here.
This role may not be a fit if
You're still building Ashby fluency. This role leans on already knowing Ashby well, since you'll be teaching it from day one. If you haven't had the chance to build that hands-on depth yet, this particular role isn't the right fit.
You prefer to set strategy and hand it off. This is a hands-on role. You'll be the one scoping, writing, recording, and shipping, not directing someone else to do it.
You need a fully defined scope before you can do your best work. You'll often be the one deciding what shape an asset takes and how deep to take it, without a fully mapped plan.
You'd rather optimize an established system than help shape one. You'll have the chance to define how this program works and put your stamp on the approach, building something you're proud of rather than fine-tuning what's already set.
You want a coordination or project-management role. This is a maker seat. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself, not managing a queue of other people's.
You measure success by how much content ships. We care about whether the right education gets built and whether customers actually use it: engagement, progress, adoption of the workflows it supports, and reduced dependence on 1:1 support are all signs that the work is landing.
You're energized by large, highly structured teams. You'll often be responsible for identifying where structure is needed and putting it in place yourself

Au sein de l'équipe Digital / IT Client Solutions, nous recherchons un(e) Manager ITCS Delivery Excellence passionné(e) par la transformation des organisations, la performance opérationnelle et la création de valeur.
Dans ce rôle stratégique, vous contribuez à faire évoluer les modes de delivery de nos équipes afin d'accroître durablement leur performance, leur efficacité et leur impact pour le Business et les utilisateurs. Véritable catalyseur du changement, vous accompagnez les équipes dans l'adoption de nouvelles pratiques, le développement de leurs compétences et l'ancrage d'une culture fondée sur la collaboration, la responsabilisation et la recherche permanente de progrès.
Vous jouez un rôle clé dans l'alignement entre stratégie, priorités, exécution et résultats. À travers une approche pragmatique et orientée impact, vous contribuez à construire une organisation plus performante, plus agile et plus orientée client.
Vous faîtes évoluer les pratiques, les standards de pilotage et les modes de fonctionnement en vous appuyant sur les principes Agile et Lean. À ce titre, vous contribuez à simplifier les processus, fluidifier les flux de travail et renforcer l'excellence opérationnelle de notre équipe.
Grâce à votre expertise, vous mettez en place des mécanismes de pilotage data-driven et visuels (Obeya, KPIs, tableaux de bord) afin de favoriser une prise de décision rapide et éclairée. Vous encouragez également les approches centrées utilisateur, l-observation terrain (Gemba), l-empathie client et l-automatisation des processus pour améliorer en continu l-expérience utilisateur et et la qualité des services délivrés.
Enfin, vous contribuez à renforcer la capacité de Digital / IT Client Solutions à concrétiser ses ambitions stratégiques en transformant les priorités en résultats tangibles et durables.

* Vous justifiez d-au moins 10 ans d-expérience dans le pilotage d-organisations IT, de portefeuilles de projets ou de fonctions Delivery Excellence, avec une expérience significative en transformation des modes de fonctionnement et dans un environnement international
* Vous possédez une solide expérience dans l-amélioration de la performance opérationnelle, la mise en œuvre de pratiques Agile, Lean ou DevOps, ainsi que dans l-optimisation des processus et des organisations
* Vous avez une forte orientation client et utilisateur, et avez déjà mis en œuvre des approches centrées sur les besoins métiers, l-observation terrain et/ou le Design centré utilisateur
* Vous maîtrisez les approches de gouvernance, de pilotage data-driven, les indicateurs de performance et les outils de management visuel (Obeya ou équivalent)
* Vous disposez d-une expérience confirmée dans la gestion budgétaire, la construction de business cases, l-optimisation de la valeur et le pilotage de fournisseurs stratégiques
* Vous êtes reconnu(e) pour vos compétences de leadership, votre capacité à fédérer des équipes pluridisciplinaires et à accompagner la montée en maturité des organisations
* Vous possédez d-excellentes compétences en communication, en influence et en facilitation, vous permettant d-interagir efficacement avec des interlocuteurs opérationnels comme exécutifs

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own client projects from first discovery call to final delivery — with a twist: this is a hands-on role. You won't just manage the work; you'll build a significant part of it yourself in Airtable.
Think of it as the intersection of three skills: understanding how a business operates, managing a project to done, and configuring the system with your own hands. If you've ever been the person at your company who "figured out the tools" and ended up running the whole process, this role was built for you.
A dedicated Engineer covers custom code — you cover everything else: the client, the plan, and the build.

Own the client: Be the primary point of contact for a portfolio of enterprise clients. Lead discovery, manage expectations, and turn business goals into concrete requirements.
Run the project: Own scope, priorities, and timelines. Coordinate day-to-day execution with our Engineer and keep momentum consistent across accounts.
Build in Airtable: Configure tables, automations, and interfaces yourself. You're not writing code, but you are building the system.
Make systems better: Review existing client implementations and improve their structure, usability, and scalability.

Project leadership with your hands in the work. Experience running client-facing or cross-functional projects where you also built or configured the solution — not just tracked tickets.
A power-user profile. You've mastered tools like Airtable, Notion, Asana, HubSpot, Zapier, or similar — deeply enough to design processes in them, not just use them.
Comfort with structured data. You get how tables relate to each other and why clean structure keeps a growing system from breaking. Formal database training is a plus rather than a prerequisite.
Strong communication. You can lead a meeting with executives and translate between business and technical worlds.
Accountability. You own outcomes across multiple projects at once and don't wait to be told what's next.

Airtable experience (a big plus — but we'll train the right builder).
Background in consulting, agencies, RevOps, or operations.
Familiarity with the low-code/no-code ecosystem.
Experience with ClickUp.

Full-time (40 hours/week), fully remote. This is a core client-facing role: you'll need stable, dedicated availability aligned with US business hours.

Zayo’s communications infrastructure solutions include dark fiber, private data networks, wavelengths, Ethernet, and dedicated Internet access. Zayo serves wireless and wireline carriers, media, tech, content, finance, healthcare and other large enterprises.
The Senior Program Manager, Long Haul OSP Deployment is responsible for the strategic leadership and successful delivery of Zayo's long haul fiber deployment portfolio through direct oversight of turnkey engineering and construction partners, cross-functional leadership, and governance of multiple concurrent, large-scale infrastructure programs. This role provides both strategic direction and operational execution across complex, multi-million-dollar network expansion initiatives.
The Senior Program Manager owns program governance, capital planning, contractor strategy, executive stakeholder alignment, risk management, and portfolio performance while ensuring projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with Zayo quality standards.
Serving as the primary operational and contractual interface between Zayo, engineering and construction partners, customers, and executive leadership, this position drives organizational alignment across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, Regulatory, GIS, and Network Planning to deliver critical network infrastructure at scale.
This role also leads continuous improvement initiatives, establishes deployment best practices, mentors program managers, and influences long-term deployment strategy across the Long Haul organization.
The Senior Program Manager reports to the Director, Long Haul OSP Deployment.

Own a portfolio of large-scale long haul deployment programs supporting strategic network expansion initiatives.
Develop portfolio delivery strategies aligned with company growth objectives and capital investment priorities.
Lead cross-functional planning from business case development through engineering, permitting, construction, testing, customer acceptance, and operational turnover.
Establish program governance, delivery standards, performance metrics, and executive reporting across multiple concurrent initiatives.
Balance competing priorities, resources, and funding across multiple programs to optimize delivery performance.
Identify portfolio-level risks and dependencies and proactively implement mitigation and recovery strategies.
Provide recommendations to senior leadership regarding delivery strategy, capital allocation, contractor utilization, and execution priorities.

Build trusted relationships with executive leadership, customers, regulatory agencies, and strategic construction partners.
Lead executive steering committees, program reviews, and customer governance meetings.
Influence cross-functional decision making across Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations, Legal, Regulatory Affairs, and Network Planning.
Drive alignment between business objectives and deployment execution across multiple organizations.

Develop long-term strategic relationships with turnkey engineering and construction partners.
Lead commercial negotiations for engineering and construction agreements, amendments, and complex change orders.
Establish contractor performance scorecards, KPIs, governance processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Evaluate contractor capacity, financial performance, safety metrics, production trends, and quality performance.
Drive executive-level performance reviews and corrective action plans when contractor performance falls below expectations.
Partner with Procurement and Legal to optimize sourcing strategies and improve contractor performance across the deployment portfolio.
Portfolio Financial Management
Own portfolio-level capital planning, forecasting, and financial performance.
Manage multi-million-dollar capital budgets across numerous concurrent deployment programs.
Lead financial forecasting, variance analysis, accrual management, and executive reporting.
Evaluate commercial impacts of scope changes, schedule adjustments, and risk events.
Partner with Finance to improve forecasting accuracy and optimize capital deployment.
Identify opportunities for cost savings, operational efficiencies, and improved return on investment.
Engineering, Regulatory & Deployment Governance

Leverage program data and performance metrics to improve forecasting accuracy, contractor productivity, and deployment efficiency.
Drive lessons learned across the organization to continuously improve delivery performance.

Project Manager, Client Onboarding
CrelioHealth Inc. · Remote (United States) · Full-time · Travel to client sites (~25–40%)
Compensation: $95,000 – $120,000 base, depending on experience + performance incentives (including incentives on expansion or referral opportunities you help close). Benefits include health coverage and PTO.
About CrelioHealth
CrelioHealth builds cloud-based laboratory information systems (LIS/LIMS) that power diagnostic labs across the United States and 2,500+ labs worldwide. Our platform runs the full lab workflow — from order booking and specimen tracking through result reporting, patient engagement, billing, and inventory — for physician office labs, hospital labs, reference labs, and direct-to-consumer testing companies. We are HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified, and growing quickly in the US market.

When a lab signs with CrelioHealth , you are the person who turns that signature into a running lab. You will own client onboarding end to end: planning the implementation, configuring the rollout with our product and support teams, training lab staff, managing the go-live, and making sure the client is delighted enough to expand and refer. You are the face of CrelioHealth from kickoff to steady state.
This is not a sales role. You carry no quota and you will never cold-call. But onboarding is where trust is built, and trust is where growth comes from. We want someone who can confidently present the platform, handle a skeptical lab director, and spot the moment a client is ready for another module or another location — and who earns incentives when those opportunities convert.

Lead onboarding projects for new US clients — single-site labs through multi-location networks — from kickoff through go-live and handover to support.
Build and run the implementation plan: scope, milestones, data migration, instrument interfaces, integrations (EHR/EMR, billing, HL7/FHIR), user setup, and validation.
Coordinate internal teams (product, engineering, support) and client stakeholders (lab directors, pathologists, techs, front-desk, billing, IT) to keep every go-live on schedule.
Travel to client sites for kickoffs, go-lives, and training — roughly 25–40% of your time, varying with the project calendar.
Make clients successful
Train lab staff on real workflows — accessioning, worklists, QC, reporting, patient portal — and adapt the training to how each lab actually operates.
Anticipate and manage change resistance: a lab switching its LIS is changing how everyone works, and you will guide them through it.
Track onboarding health (time-to-go-live, adoption, early ticket volume) and report status honestly to clients and leadership.
Champion the platform
Present and demo CrelioHealth confidently — to the client team that signed, and to the wider staff who did not choose it but must love it.
Identify expansion opportunities during onboarding (additional modules, locations, or referrals) and hand them to the growth team — with incentives for you when they close.
Feed what you learn on the ground back into product and our onboarding playbook, which you will help write.

4–7 years of project management experience , with at least 2 years implementing or onboarding software for external clients.
Healthcare experience is required ; hands-on time in a clinical laboratory or laboratory environment is strongly preferred — as a lab tech, lab manager, LIS analyst, or implementer of lab systems (LIS/LIMS, EHR, RCM).
Fluency with lab operations concepts: specimen lifecycle, accessioning, QC/QA, instrument interfacing, CLIA/CAP context, HIPAA, and result reporting.
Excellent presenter and communicator — comfortable running a room of skeptical clinicians, and equally comfortable on a video call with a solo lab owner.
Structured and self-managing: you can run multiple concurrent onboardings remotely without anyone chasing you.
Willingness to travel to client sites across the US; valid driver’s license and authorization to work in the United States.
Nice-to-haves
Direct experience with an LIS/LIMS migration or go-live (any vendor).
Familiarity with HL7v2 / FHIR interfaces, lab billing/RCM basics, or instrument middleware.
Experience in customer success, solutions consulting, or pre-sales — anywhere you have had to win people over, not just manage tasks.
PMP, CAPM, or Lean Six Sigma is welcome but not required — we care more about go-lives you have shipped than certificates you hold.
Comfort using modern AI tools to work faster (drafting plans, summarizing calls, preparing training material) — with the judgment to know what still needs a human.
How We Hire
We know polished resumes and cover letters are easy to generate these days, so our process is built around watching you work rather than reading about it. After a screening call, you will do a live onboarding simulation based on a realistic lab scenario, and a short role-play where you present CrelioHealth to a (friendly but skeptical) “lab director.” No trick questions, no take-home busywork — just the actual job, compressed. We will respect your time and give you a decision quickly.
The Fine Print
CrelioHealth Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
The salary range above is a good-faith estimate for this posting and may vary based on experience, skills, and location within the US.
